title: David Protein founder's candy launch is full of AI typos. The brand's president says it's intentional 'rage bait.'
excerpt: "We left them there for a little bit of internet rage bait," HallPass president Michael Tierney told Business Insider. "It's worked."
content_html:
By Henry Chandonnet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

In HallPass' product shot, sugar is "suger," and package is "pacaage."

The lower-calorie candy company comes from some big names in food. Its cofounders are Peter Rahal, the cofounder of David Protein and RxBar, and Michael Tierney, the founder of Stuffed Puffs. It also operates under Medici Brands, David Protein's parent company.

And yet, its Monday launch was full of AI flubs.

Much of the text is a blurred garble of letters. Take the words under "peanut creme crispy waters" (they were going for "wafers"). They're completely incoherent, a classic example of AI image generators' well-documented struggle to replicate text.

Or there's the "…Have Fun" above the logo. The middle bar has an extra dot in the ellipsis. The bottom bar swaps an H for an N.

Other images show this says "enlarged for detail." But does it really look like that?

Eagle-eyed viewers called out the typos online. Casey Lewis, author of the After School newsletter, said that "copy editors have never been more important" in the age of AI.

Two days after the launch, Tierney told Business Insider that the flubs were intentional. HallPass had individual images of the three bars, he said, but none of them together. In Tierney's telling, they used AI to combine the images, and immediately saw the issues.

"We left them there for a little bit of internet rage bait," he said. "It's worked."

Tierney pointed to the product's name, HallPass. The AI flubs were another nod to the fact that "this is a fun brand," he said.

Brands using AI in their advertising has proven risky and prone to backlash. REI was roasted for its AI use after an ad showed two sets of bicycle handlebars. A bagel shop owner told Business Insider how using AI in his Instagram posts tanked his Google reviews.

AI pessimism is on the rise, and some commenters online took HallPass' typos as an offense. Tierney said he wasn't worried; he said that he was trying to drive some "top-of-funnel awareness" for the launch.

HallPass candies will launch in Walmart stores across the US on August 29. Tierney promises there won't be any typos on those bars.

在 HallPass 的产品镜头中，糖是“suger”，包装是“pacaage”。

低热量糖果公司出自食品界的一些大牌。 其联合创始人是David Protein和RxBar的联合创始人Peter Rahal和Stuffed Puffs的创始人Michael Tierney。 该公司还在 David Protein 的母公司 Medici Brands 旗下运营。

然而，周一的发布却充满了人工智能的失误。

大部分文字都是模糊的字母乱码。 就拿“花生奶油脆水”下面的词来说吧（他们本来是指“威化饼”）。 它们完全不连贯，这是人工智能图像生成器复制文本的斗争的典型例子。

或者徽标上方有“……玩得开心”。 中间栏的省略号中有一个额外的点。 底部栏将 H 替换为 N。

其他图像显示这上面写着“放大细节”。 但看起来真的是这样吗？

眼尖的观众在网上指出了这些错别字。 《After School》时事通讯的作者凯西·刘易斯 (Casey Lewis) 表示，在人工智能时代，“文案编辑从未如此重要”。

发布两天后，蒂尔尼告诉《商业内幕》，这些失误是故意的。 他说，HallPass 拥有这三个酒吧的单独图片，但没有一张放在一起。 据蒂尔尼讲述，他们使用人工智能来组合图像，并立即发现了问题。

他说：“我们把它们留在那里，只是为了引起网络愤怒。” “成功了。”

蒂尔尼指着产品的名称：HallPass。 他说，人工智能的失误再次证明了“这是一个有趣的品牌”这一事实。

事实证明，在广告中使用人工智能的品牌存在风险，并且容易遭到强烈反对。 REI 在广告中展示了两套自行车车把后，因其人工智能的使用而受到批评。 一位百吉饼店老板告诉《商业内幕》，在他的 Instagram 帖子中使用人工智能如何降低了他在谷歌上的评价。

人工智能的悲观情绪正在上升，一些网上评论者认为 HallPass 的拼写错误是一种冒犯。 蒂尔尼说他并不担心。他说，他正在努力为这次发布提高一些“漏斗顶部的意识”。

HallPass 糖果将于 8 月 29 日在美国各地的沃尔玛商店上市。 蒂尔尼承诺这些条上不会出现任何拼写错误。
